question.worked_solution:
From the definition of $f(x),$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -3}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to -3}((a-x)^{2}-a) \\  & =(a+3)^{2}-a \\  & ={a}^{2}+5a+9.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=-3,$ we must have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -3}f(x) & =f(-3) \\ {a}^{2}+5a+9 & =9 \\ {a}^{2}+5a & =0 \\ a(a+5) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, $a=-5$ or $a=0.$
